\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مسافة} (masāfa)}{مسافة (masāfa)}]{\ar{مسافة} (masāfa) — a distance}

\label{lesson:AR-C427-masafa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to empty out, then the Arabic for to confiscate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مسافة}}
\textbf{\ar{مسافة}} — \emph{masāfa} — \textquotedblleft{}a distance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{المسافة} \ar{من} \ar{القرية} \ar{إلى} \ar{المدينة} \ar{قصيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{al-masāfa min al-qarya ilā al-madīna qaṣīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The distance from the village to the city is short.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مسافة}} (\emph{masāfa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-w-f}, \textquotedblleft{}to smell\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane records the old account: a desert guide smelled the ground to know the way, so the stretch he sniffed out was a \emph{masāfa}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{masāfa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{masāfa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{al-masāfa min al-qarya ilā al-madīna qaṣīra.} — The distance from the village to the city is short.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to empty out, then the Arabic for to confiscate, then say \emph{masāfa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مسافة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A distance\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تأكد} (taʾakkada)}{تأكد (taʾakkada)}]{\ar{تأكد} (taʾakkada) — to make sure}

\label{lesson:AR-C427-taakkada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to confiscate, then the Arabic for a distance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تأكد}}
\textbf{\ar{تأكد}} — \emph{taʾakkada} — \textquotedblleft{}to make sure\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تأكد} \ar{أبي} \ar{من} \ar{الحجز}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taʾakkada abī min al-ḥajz.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father made sure of the booking.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتأكد}, \emph{yataʾakkad}.

It takes \emph{min}: \emph{taʾakkada min}, \textquotedblleft{}to make sure of\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تأكد}} (\emph{taʾakkada}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʾ-k-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to make firm\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, \textquotedblleft{}to become firm in one's mind\textquotedblright{}; \emph{mutaʾakkid}, \textquotedblleft{}sure\textquotedblright{}, is its participle.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to confiscate, then the Arabic for a distance, then say \emph{taʾakkada} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عدل} (ʿaddala)}{عدل (ʿaddala)}]{\ar{عدل} (ʿaddala) — to adjust; to modify}

\label{lesson:AR-C427-addala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a distance, then the Arabic for to make sure.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عدل}}
\textbf{\ar{عدل}} — \emph{ʿaddala} — \textquotedblleft{}to adjust; to modify\textquotedblright{}.

\end{quote}

\textbf{\ar{عدل}} (\emph{ʿaddala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-d-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to be even, balanced\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II, \textquotedblleft{}to make even, to set straight\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for getting around.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استأجر} (istaʾjara)}{استأجر (istaʾjara)}]{\ar{استأجر} (istaʾjara) — to hire; to rent (from someone)}

\label{lesson:AR-C427-istajara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to make sure, then the Arabic for to adjust.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استأجر}}
\textbf{\ar{استأجر}} — \emph{istaʾjara} — \textquotedblleft{}to hire; to rent (from someone)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{استأجرنا} \ar{سيارة} \ar{صغيرة} \ar{في} \ar{المطار}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{istaʾjarnā sayyāra ṣaghīra fī al-maṭār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We hired a small car at the airport.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يستأجر}, \emph{yastaʾjir}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استأجر}} (\emph{istaʾjara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʾ-j-r}, \textquotedblleft{}a wage, a reward\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form X, \textquotedblleft{}to take something for a payment\textquotedblright{}; \emph{ījār}, \textquotedblleft{}rent\textquotedblright{}, shares the root.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for getting around.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حقيبة} \ar{ظهر} (ḥaqībat ẓahr)}{حقيبة ظهر (ḥaqībat ẓahr)}]{\ar{حقيبة} \ar{ظهر} (ḥaqībat ẓahr) — a backpack}

\label{lesson:AR-C427-haqibat-zahr}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to adjust, then the Arabic for to hire.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حقيبة} \ar{ظهر}}
\textbf{\ar{حقيبة} \ar{ظهر}} — \emph{ḥaqībat ẓahr} — \textquotedblleft{}a backpack\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{حمل} \ar{أخي} \ar{حقيبة} \ar{ظهر} \ar{كبيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḥamala akhī ḥaqībat ẓahr kabīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother carried a big backpack.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حقيبة} \ar{ظهر}} (\emph{ḥaqībat ẓahr}) is built from two native Arabic words: \emph{ḥaqība}, \textquotedblleft{}a bag\textquotedblright{}, on the root \emph{ḥ-q-b} (Lane), and \emph{ẓahr}, \textquotedblleft{}the back\textquotedblright{}, on the root \emph{ẓ-h-r} (Lane): a bag for the back.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}
